abstraction_design.rationale: The data helpers stretch well, but the card component accretes per-page flags and the route skeleton is duplicated rather than shared — a new section copies boilerplate instead of reusing it.

findings.issue: The home page re-implements Pokémon-card construction (sprite, slot-sorted types) instead of reusing speciesCards, so card-level rules exist in two places (species-cards.ts:41 vs index.ts:125).
findings.suggestion: Extract a cardFromPokemonRecord(record) helper into lib/species-cards.ts and have both the home handler and speciesCards use it.

findings.issue: Every document/template function casts context.props.GET as any (10 occurrences across the five routes), throwing away the prop typing defineRoute infers from the handler return.
findings.suggestion: Give each handler's return a named exported type and drop the casts, so renaming a prop fails at compile time in the template that consumes it.

findings.issue: The url.hostname === 'gracile-static' build-time stub guard is repeated in five handlers with inconsistent stub shapes (index returns full empty props, the others return notFound), so a framework change means five edits.
findings.suggestion: Add a shared isBuildStub(url) (or withBuildStub(props)) helper in lib and use one documented stub shape everywhere.

findings.issue: The alternate-form exclusion rule is inlined as id <= 10000 here while the canonical isAlternateForm helper lives in app/src/lib/format.ts:63 and is used by speciesCards.
findings.suggestion: Use isAlternateForm (or a notAlternateForm wrapper) so the 10000 threshold has a single definition.

findings.issue: CardData is a union-by-flag of three page contexts (speciesName/speciesId, optional types, optional hiddenAbility), each documented as 'home page only'/'ability page only'; a new card variant means another optional field on a shared struct.
findings.suggestion: Either split into cardList(cards, { types?: (c)=>..., extra?: (c)=>TemplateResult }) style per-context slots, or keep the base card pure and let callers compose extra slots into the anchor.

findings.issue: The filter query-parameter contract (q, type, generation, page; omit defaults) is duplicated between the server's pageUrl (index.ts:26-37) and the client's navigate(), so adding a filter means editing both.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared buildFilterUrl(filters, page) used by both server template and client script (the client script is plain TS and can import from src/lib).

findings.issue: Damage-relation links hand-roll the type-badge markup (class type-badge type-${name}, /types/ href, humanize) that typeBadge(name, true) in components.ts:17 already encapsulates.
findings.suggestion: Reuse typeBadge(t.name, true) inside the map and keep the space-joining outside, so badge styling/URL rules stay in one place.

findings.issue: All ~560 lines of styling live in one global stylesheet with per-route class prefixes, so removing a feature leaves dead CSS behind and unrelated pages share one edit surface.
findings.suggestion: Gracile supports per-route sibling styles (route .css files imported by the route); at minimum move per-page blocks (abilities-list, moves-table, pokemon-hero, damage-relations) into sibling route styles.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Gracile/Lit codebase: five thin route entry points over a small, well-factored lib (api, format, species-cards, components) plus one shared document, so most change scenarios touch one or two obvious files. The standout wart is the home page bypassing the speciesCards abstraction to rebuild card data, which makes sprite/ordering bugs a two-place fix, followed by the universal `as any` casts that discard defineRoute's prop typing. Features are otherwise trivially removable and the API base URL/caching rules have exactly one owner, which is what a team inheriting this repo wants.
